text:
The Rangers lost Igor Shesterkin for the season on Oct. 9, and the month since has been one long audition in net. Dylan Garand carried most of it (12 of 18 starts), James Reimer came and went through unconditional waivers, and Joonas Korpisalo, acquired from Boston in July, finally made his debut Saturday in Seattle and won it. Tonight he gets Edmonton. That is a lot to ask of a goalie who finished last season 2.46 goals worse than his shots deserved over 31 games.

The better news for New York is that the skaters have stopped needing a rescue. Three straight wins, and the chances back them: 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count) across those games. Sean Durzi is on injured reserve, so Braden Schneider has moved in beside Marcus Pettersson and Adam Fox is up to 24:32 a night. Alexis Lafrenière, two assists Saturday, is the name our numbers flag as both breaking out and due.

The Oilers are 12-3-3 and first in the Pacific, but read the fine print. They are +21 in goal difference on +5.4 expected, with finishing (about 19 goals more than their chances usually produce) doing the lifting. Connor McDavid has an 18-game point streak (10 goals, 37 assists), Leon Draisaitl has goals in three straight and Evan Bouchard has points in six. All three carry our "due to cool" tag, which is less a forecast than a reminder that nobody shoots like this forever. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins took a teammate's shoot-in off the side of the head Saturday; Mike Babcock didn't think he would miss much time, but his status is unclear. Devon Levi, back from injury, is at .888 in eight games.

Our numbers call it close: 3.11 expected goals for Edmonton, 2.93 for New York. The Oilers won the first meeting 4-1 on Nov. 1, a game they deserved 58% of the time.
headline: Korpisalo's second test is the hardest one

hunch.text: The Rangers have been the better five-on-five team for a week and the Oilers' finishing can't stay this hot. Our gut says New York wins in Edmonton.
